title: Controlling GLP-1 Waste with Dietitian-Led Care
summary: GLP-1 spend is costly when it doesn’t turn into lasting results, and waste concentrates at three points in the medication journey: starting medication unnecessarily, stopping early, and restarting after weight regain.
body_markdown:
GLP-1 medications have changed what’s possible in treating obesity and metabolic disease, but they come with a significant price tag. At an estimated $9,600 per patient per year, stakeholders across the healthcare ecosystem are increasingly concerned about whether that spend turns into lasting results.


A new analysis compares Nourish patient outcomes with published real-world benchmarks to estimate where dietitian-led care plays a role in helping keep that spend from going to waste. Nourish offers three GLP-1 care pathways (nutrition-first, companion, and off-ramp), with each personalized to the health history and goals of patients interested in medication. Each pathway helps to avoid GLP-1 waste through a different mechanism.


**Nutrition-first:** 10% of Nourish patients are on a GLP-1, compared with 23% of U.S. adults with overweight or obesity; with dietitians as the first touchpoint of care, medication is used only when it’s clinically appropriate. That gap accounts for the largest share of the estimated waste avoidance, at $1,248 per patient.


**Companion:** Patients on GLP-1s are more likely to discontinue early when side effects and everyday questions go unaddressed. With regular dietitian support and daily tracking between visits, 76% of Nourish patients who start a GLP-1 are still on it at six months, compared with the 61% seen in real-world data. Staying on treatment long enough for it to work is worth an estimated $360 in waste avoidance per patient.


**Off-ramp:** Coming off of a GLP-1 poses its own risks, including weight regain. With dietitian support through this transition, 64% of Nourish patients maintain weight loss 12 months after discontinuing, compared with 49% in real-world data. Fewer patients losing ground means fewer second courses of medication, and an estimated $576 in waste avoidance per patient.


Much of the value that GLP-1s can deliver is contingent on factors outside of the prescription itself, including who gets one, how long it’s used, and what happens when it ends. A registered dietitian at the center of care ensures medication gets used only when it’s needed, for as long as it’s working, and with a plan for what comes next.


Read the full analysis[here](https://d3f4micfw8j9t2.cloudfront.net/blog/GLP-1%20Waste%20Avoidance%20(November%202026).pdf) .
